summary: @ornikar/eslint-plugin-neverthrow preinstall fetches Bun runtime to execute obfuscated payload
details: The package's npm preinstall hook runs setup.mjs, which downloads a Bun runtime binary from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases, extracts it to a temp directory, chmod+x's it, and then invokes that binary to execute a package-local file named math_init.js. math_init.js is a ~727 KB single-line, heavily obfuscated script (hex-mangled identifiers, numeric string-array with a rotate/lookup decoder such as WV8StW / n7gIxM, `// @bun @bun-cjs` header) whose contents cannot be read by scanners that only inspect Node-resolved code. An ESLint plugin has no legitimate need to fetch a second language runtime at install time to execute an opaque bundled payload; this shape is an alternate-runtime dropper used to evade static analysis. The preinstall path runs automatically on `npm install`, so any installer of this version executes the obfuscated payload under Bun on their machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
